episodes.194553: Widespread slow-moving showers with moderate rain led to continued areas of flash flooding across the Permian Basin.
episodes.194718: Several strong thunderstorms moved up the Bitterroot Valley into Southwest Montana during the late morning and early afternoon hours. These storms produced gusty outflow winds and small hail.
episodes.194849: A few thunderstorms produced some severe wind gusts. This was a result of large temperature/dewpoint spreads.
episodes.194930: A thunderstorm briefly became severe east of Oelrichs, producing wind gusts up to 65 mph.
episodes.195030: Convection formed in the vicinity of a stationary front over South-Central Texas. Thunderstorms developed in an anomalously moist airmass with weak steering flow. This led to slow moving, heavy rain producing cells and flash flooding.
episodes.195270: A shortwave trough brushed across northern Utah, resulting in enough support for the development of scattered high-based thunderstorms. A few of these thunderstorms produced instances of severe level wind gusts.
episodes.195271: A shortwave trough brushed across southern Wyoming, resulting in enough support for the development of scattered high-based thunderstorms, and isolated severe level wind gusts.
episodes.195455: A shortwave trough brought strong thunderstorms with high winds to the West Central Mountains and Treasure Valley.
episodes.195832: A funnel cloud was reported over the St Johns River west of Cocoa.
episodes.195878: A series of upper level shortwaves passed across Montana during the day on both September 2 and 3. This aided in thunderstorm formation in an environment marginally favorable for severe hail, and favorable for strong wind gusts (Deep inverted-V soundings). Only two severe caliber reports were received from these thunderstorms.
episodes.196019: A low pressure system off the coast of northern California formed a small upper level trough that moved over northern Nevada. Mid-level moisture associated with the front caused isolated thunderstorms to form that created high level wind gusts.
episodes.196125: A front was stalled across NE FL with a meandering coastal low offshore of the local Atlantic coast. Above normal atmospheric moisture, warm temperatures aloft and slow storm motion produced localized heavy rainfall over a diurnally unstable airmass with waves of gusty showers moving onshore. Wind gusts with the coastal low along the local Atlantic coast increased to 40-50 mph after 8 pm on 9/3 through midnight along the Duval County FL coast.
episodes.196126: A front was stalled across NE FL with a meandering coastal low offshore of the local Atlantic coast. Above normal atmospheric moisture, warm temperatures aloft and slow storm motion produced localized heavy rainfall over a diurnally unstable airmass with waves of gusty showers moving onshore. Wind gusts with the coastal low along the local Atlantic coast increased to 40-50 mph after 8 pm on 9/3 through midnight along the Duval County FL coast.
episodes.196249: An influx of deep tropical moisture associated with a weak upper level disturbance and associated low pressure system along the Lower Texas coast provided daily, mainly afternoon showers and thunderstorms between September 2 and 5. The precipitation favored the lower Valley (Cameron/Willacy County).  On the 3rd, a resident of Harlingen reported a direct cloud-to-ground lightning strike on her home which resulted in damage.
episodes.196470: As a surface frontal boundary pushed southward through the southeastern United States, winds began to veer south-southeast bringing moist, warm air into South Florida. This supported the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms across the area throughout the day.
episodes.196471: As a surface frontal boundary pushed southward through the southeastern United States, winds began to veer south-southeast bringing moist, warm air into South Florida. This supported the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms across the area throughout the day.
episodes.196567: A cold front crossed Wyoming and brought scattered thunderstorms. Some storms contained high wind gusts. Severe wind gusts were reported at the Greybull, Worland, and Sweetwater County airport. The highest wind gust was 66 mph at the Sweetwater County Airport.
episodes.196573: A significant heavy rainfall event occurred early in the month across mainly the Concho Valley, northern Heartland and southern Big Country due to a slow moving upper level storm system and a very moist tropical airmass, which was near record levels for early September. Numerous showers and a few thunderstorms produced localized heavy rainfall amounts greater than 10 inches across portions of northeast Tom Green, southwest Runnels and northern Concho counties which resulted in significant areal and flash flooding.
episodes.196610: Thunderstorms producing heavy rain impacted areas of North Texas during the morning hours on Sept 3rd and produced flooding in Tarrant County.
episodes.196619: Extreme eastern Idaho received some flash flooding and severe winds.
episodes.196783: As a surface frontal boundary pushed southward through the southeastern United States, winds began to veer south-southeast bringing moist, warm air into South Florida. This supported the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms across the area throughout the day.

This was a report from mPING indicating potential road closures.

Broadcast media reported a partial roof collapse in a duplex near Northeast 10th Avenue and Second Street in Hallandale Beach after heavy rainfall impacted the area. Rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches were observed in the area.

At 735 AM CDT, the Tom Green County Sheriff Office received a call about a vehicle truck that was swept away by swift water currents in the flooded area of McMillan and Wright Roads in northeastern Tom Green County. The truck was swept approximately 150 yards from the roadway, to near a tree. The cab of the truck was submerged, and the occupants were clinging to the tree above the flood waters. All of the 5 victims were successfully rescued by first responders from the Tom Green County Sheriff Office and the San Angelo Fire Department. The Texas Department of Public Safety and Texas Parks and Wildlife Department were also involved in the rescue efforts.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding closing Hwy 83 south of Catarina.

Local media reported lightning damaging a home in West Park. The lightning struck the pavement outside the home, which then traveled up a metal fence and shot through the ceiling into a bedroom where a 1-year-old baby was sleeping, causing the roof to collapse. No injuries were reported. Time is based on National Lightning Detection Network data which showed several lightning strikes in the immediate area. Damage totals are estimated.

Gusty outflow occurred throughout the Bitterroot Valley but a localized area from just south of Corvallis to near Quast Lane experienced damaging winds. A few downed trees and numerous downed branches were noted.  A peak gusts of 63 mph occurred at Soft Rock RAWS which was supported by radar velocities with 2000-3000 customers losing power.
A significant amount of water was covering FM 1298 south of Lake J.B. Thomas.

A resident of central Harlingen reported a direct lightning strike to the home.  Approximate time is based on the report, which noted that the strike came just before torrential rains that were also reported at nearby Valley International Airport (2.4 miles to the east-northeast). Damage included roof and decking blown out and underlaying PVC pipe damage.  No fire was reported.
